items.passage: Under the Air Passenger Protection Regulations (SOR/2019-150), a large carrier must pay $400 in compensation for an arrival delay of more than three hours but less than six hours that is within its control.

items.strategy: wrong time anchor (arrival delay to departure delay)
items.why: The compensation bands are measured by arrival delay at the final destination, not by departure delay.
items.passage: Under the Air Passenger Protection Regulations (SOR/2019-150), a large carrier must pay $400 in compensation for a departure delay of three hours or more but less than six hours that is within its control.

items.why: The regulation contains no 24-hour claim window; the condition is invented.
items.passage: Under the Air Passenger Protection Regulations (SOR/2019-150), a large carrier must pay $400 in compensation for an arrival delay of three hours or more but less than six hours that is within its control, payable only if the passenger submits a claim within 24 hours of arrival.

Where an arrival delay of at least three hours but under six hours is within its control, a large carrier owes a compensation payment of $400 under the Air Passenger Protection Regulations (SOR/2019-150).

items.why: The short-term right to terminate applies to goods that do not conform, not to services.
items.passage: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2022 (Ireland), a consumer has a short-term right to terminate a contract for the supply of services that do not conform, exercisable within 30 days of delivery.

items.why: The 30-day period runs from delivery of the goods, not from signing the contract.
items.passage: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2022 (Ireland), a consumer has a short-term right to terminate a sales contract for goods that do not conform, exercisable within 30 days of the contract being signed.

items.strategy: quantifier flip (within to no earlier than)
items.why: The right is exercisable within 30 days of delivery, and not only after that period has passed.
items.passage: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2022 (Ireland), a consumer has a short-term right to terminate a sales contract for goods that do not conform, exercisable no earlier than 30 days after delivery.
A consumer may, under the Consumer Rights Act 2022 (Ireland), exercise a short-term right to terminate a sales contract for non-conforming goods at any time within 30 days after delivery.

items.why: The erasure obligation under Article 17 is directed to the controller.
items.passage: Under Article 17 of the GDPR, the data subject has the right to obtain from the processor the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay.

items.why: Payment of a fee is not a condition of the erasure right under Article 17.
items.passage: Under Article 17 of the GDPR, the data subject has the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay, provided that the data subject has paid an administrative fee.

items.why: The GDPR's obligations applied from 25 May 2018, not from 1 January 2016.
items.passage: Under Article 17 of the GDPR, as applicable from 1 January 2016, the data subject has the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay.
Article 17 of the GDPR entitles a data subject to require that the controller erase personal data relating to them, and the controller is bound to do so without undue delay.

items.strategy: wrong time anchor (receipt of document to first seller contact)
items.why: The eight-day period runs from receipt of the written contract document, not from the seller's first contact.
items.passage: Under Japan's Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, a purchaser in a door-to-door sale may cancel the contract in writing within eight days of the first contact made by the seller.

items.why: The cooling-off right is optional for the purchaser; cancellation is not mandatory.
items.passage: Under Japan's Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, a purchaser in a door-to-door sale must cancel the contract in writing within eight days of receiving the contract document.

items.why: The eight-day written cancellation right covers door-to-door sales and similar specified transactions, not mail-order sales.
items.passage: Under Japan's Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, a purchaser in a mail-order sale may cancel the contract in writing within eight days of receiving the contract document.

Under Japan's Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, a purchaser in a door-to-door sale is entitled to cancel the contract by written notice, provided it is given within eight days from the day the written contract document is received.
